items.title: 0.1.0-rc16 — self-update channel + signed apt + branded Linux menu
items.summary: rc16 ships miner self-update (latest.json + update_hackme_miner for Linux/Windows/HackMe OS), signed apt package hackme-node on hackme.tech/apt, branded Linux app menu, and a Windows update banner in the dashboard. ISO: HackMe-OS-0.1.0-rc16-amd64.iso SHA256 9e1c0850… — verify SHA256SUMS-iso.txt before flash.
items.impact: Miners can upgrade without re-download roulette: apt upgrade hackme-node on Ubuntu/Debian, or update_hackme_miner.sh / .bat elsewhere. .env / data / logs are preserved. Operators: publish feed is https://hackme.tech/dist/latest.json

items.title: HackMe OS ISO rebuilt — ZK recovery phrase no longer in /var/log
items.summary: Security rebuild of HackMe-OS-0.1.0-rc15-amd64.iso: the Zero-Knowledge Start recovery phrase is no longer appended to world-readable /var/log. Display logging uses /var/lib/hackme/zk-wallet-display.log (0600); the phrase is shown on local TTYs for photography only. SHA256 94590a5b… supersedes the 2026-08-22 ISO (9158109d…). Win/Linux/fuzz binaries are unchanged; hub audit hardenings (task auth, fuzz rate limits, settle fail-closed, trusted XFF, CORS) are live on hackme.tech.
items.impact: Anyone flashing from GitHub or hackme.tech downloads must re-verify SHA256SUMS-iso.txt. Old USB sticks with the Aug 22 image still leak the phrase into logs until re-flashed.

items.title: 0.1.0-rc15 LIVE — B2B fuzz Phase 2, pool anticheat, mining dashboard refresh
items.summary: rc15 is the production cut for customer fuzz on the public pool: wizard packs (secrets, script_bounds, filter_utf8, parser_expat), Scan/Audit/Deep tiers with honest byte ceilings (256 / 1K / 4K), dynamic worker leases, exec cap 64 per unit, and coverage bitmap @ WASM offset 8192. The libheif OSS research series is archived CLEAN (~2.57B exec); the #mining dashboard now prioritizes live B2B bootstrap campaigns.
items.impact: Operators and miners: hub node 0.1.0-rc15 is live on hackme.tech. Pool fuzz anticheat is tighter (segment replay fail-closed). Customer marketplace orders from bootstrap B2B node rotate light parser targets onto the pool with PoH attach — visible on #mining. Win/Linux/fuzz SHA256SUMS match GitHub; HackMe OS ISO was security-rebuilt 2026-08-27 (see newer news item).
items.action: Downloads: https://hackme.tech/downloads.html · GitHub: https://github.com/jokeez/hackme/releases/tag/0.1.0-rc15 · Verify SHA256SUMS.txt · News: https://hackme.tech/news.html

items.title: rc14x hotfix shipped — honest fuzz report/gate + depth evidence visible
items.summary: rc14x makes the fuzz customer reporting plane more truthful: reports now carry explicit `evidence_window` scope (fetched-window vs full-history) and disclose raw vs grouped counters (raw_findings_total, grouped_rows_visible/hidden) without changing gate/coordinator behavior.
items.impact: Customer-facing truth improvements for B2B fuzz reports: JSON/HTML/CSV now clearly separate what was fetched for this request from the full campaign history, with raw vs grouped semantics disclosed to prevent overstated totals.
items.action: Downloads: https://hackme.tech/downloads.html · GitHub: https://github.com/jokeez/hackme/releases/tag/0.1.0-rc14x · Verify SHA256SUMS.txt from the rc14x bundle.

items.title: HackMe 0.1.0-rc14 is live — pool fuzz customer-first priority
items.summary: E2E customer order flow on Aug 11: rc14 reduced claim latency from seconds to milliseconds and improved pool throughput for real customer orders. Customer order completed 256/256 in ~26 minutes; hybrid dig is ON on customer campaigns; escrow 20/80 unchanged.
items.impact: Evidence for correct pool scheduling + fuzz integration: claim path priority, customer-first ordering, and hybrid dig/fuzz runs that produce findings on customer campaigns. Not a claim of trustless L1 / exchange readiness / CEX readiness.
